problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+3{x}^{2}).$

feedback.problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, using the laws of logarithms, we observe that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2(1-\frac{x}{2})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

The Maclaurin series for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-\frac{x}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{x}{2}) & =(-\frac{x}{2})-\frac{1}{2}{(-\frac{x}{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(-\frac{x}{2})}^{3}-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{x}{2}-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})+\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{8})-⋯ \\  & =-\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the desired result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\frac{x}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2+(-\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}-⋯) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}-⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
